title: Decode scheduler hotpath heatmap aggregation and NVTX-to-kernel mapping
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Goal: produce a low-overhead, rollable telemetry surface that maps NVTX ranges and trace spans to canonical kernel IDs and aggregates per-kernel execution heatmaps across prefill and decode phases. The end product should enable the decode scheduler to make data-driven trade-offs (e.g., split-batch vs single-token fast-path) and provide SRE/engineering with hotspot dashboards and alerting for regressions.

Scope:
- Define stable kernel identifiers (name + quantization + kernel-flags) visible in traces and metrics.
- Emit lightweight per-kernel counters and time histograms with prefill vs decode phase tags.
- Correlate NVTX ranges (host-visible ranges) with kernel IDs for sampled traces to build a kernel-heatmap by sequence-length bucket.
- Create aggregated dashboards and a small API for the decode scheduler to query recent-hotpath statistics (tail latency / p99, freq).

Out of scope for this ticket: long-term storage retention policy, enterprise billing integration, and A/B rollout of scheduler changes (will be separate follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical kernel ID schema defined and documented in Confluence (one-line stable ID string)
Instrumentation added to runtime so traces include kernel ID and phase tag (prefill|decode) for sampled NVTX ranges
Lightweight per-kernel metrics (count, sum_time_ms, p50/p95 buckets) emitted to our telemetry backend for top 500 kernels
A Grafana dashboard exists showing kernel-heatmap by sequence-length buckets and phase with a linkable drilldown to example traces
A minimal HTTP endpoint (internal) returns last-5m hotspot list for a given model and device to be consumed by the decode scheduler
implementation_notes: Add per-kernel tagging in the kernel launcher so NVTX ranges attach kernel_id and phase. Avoid full NVTX range instrumentation on every call — use sampled ranges at 1% and full counters aggregated per-batch.
Emit metrics as Prometheus-style counters + histogram for latency buckets; a nightly job will import aggregates into ClickHouse for heatmap computations.
Trace sampling: enable deterministic sampling when debug flag is on (trace-more-for-model X) to reproduce hotspots; default is 1% across production traffic to limit overhead.

Correlation logic: post-process traces to map NVTX range timestamps to kernel invocations by matching device timestamps and seq offsets; conservative matching with fuzz window to handle scheduling jitter.
Storage: keep only top-N kernel aggregates per model-device tuple to cap cardinality; evict least-recently-seen kernels after 24h.
Scheduler API: basic auth internal endpoint /internal/scheduler/hotspots?model=...&device=... returning JSON list of kernel_id, p95_ms, qps. Implementation is read-only and caches responses for 15s.
Dashboard: heatmap with x-axis = seq-length-bucket, y-axis = kernel_id (grouped by op family), color = aggregated p95 latency or relative time share in phase.
Telemetry overhead targets: sampling + counters should add <2% p99 CPU overhead and <1% additional RT latency on p99 for small models; measure on canary before rollout.
Privacy: metrics contain no prompt content. Ensure traces are redacted per tracing policy and only kernel identifiers and timing are emitted.
comments: 2026-02-08 Marco Liu: Initial ticket created after perf review — kernel hotspots are opaque today and scheduler has no visibility into per-kernel tails.
2026-02-10 Anika Rao: PoC design for kernel ID schema uploaded to Confluence (link below). Recommend starting with a deterministic ID format to make heatmaps stable across releases.

2026-02-12 Sasha Nguyen (runtime): Implemented kernel-id tagging in the kernel launcher on branch feat/kernel-id-tagging; added unit tests for canonicalization. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127

2026-02-14 Marco Liu: Ran microbenchmarks — adding kernel_id to NVTX ranges increases nvtx annotations but we switch to sampled NVTX to keep overhead low. Measured ~0.8% CPU overhead with 1% sampling on a 4-GPU host.
2026-02-16 Design review (Eleni Voss): Dashboard mock looks good; suggestion to include 'time-share-in-phase' metric to understand how much of prefill vs decode each kernel consumes.

2026-02-18 Anika Rao: Implemented Prometheus counters + histogram; exporter added that aggregates per-device and pushes to ClickHouse ingest. Small follow-up PR to tune buckets. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-exporter/pull/289

2026-02-20 QA (Rajat Singh): Canary on dedicated pool showed kernel heatmap spike for attention_split_v2 at seq 4096 — filing follow-up ENG-22138 for attention tiling fallback. Marking ENG-22110 as delivering telemetry for investigation.
risks_and_mitigations: High-cardinality explosion if every kernel variant is recorded: mitigate by canonicalizing IDs and limiting top-N per model-device.
Instrumentation overhead could regress p99 latencies: mitigate with sampling, counters-only fallback, and canarying on dedicated pools before rollouts.
Mismatch between NVTX ranges and kernel boundaries on preemption: post-processing uses fuzz windows; if unreliable, fall back to host-side counters with coarser attribution.
Scheduler dependency risk: decode scheduler must handle missing hotspot data gracefully and fall back to conservative defaults.
Operational cost: ClickHouse ingest cost — cap aggregation windows and retention to control storage growth.
